title: Orange County Commission, District 2 (runoff)
what_it_does: County commissioners set the county budget and property-tax (millage) rate, adopt land-use and zoning rules, and oversee county services such as roads, parks, libraries, fire/EMS and utilities. Orange County commission seats are nonpartisan; the commission expanded to eight districts for 2026.
verified_ballot_note: Runoff per Florida Politics (https://floridapolitics.com/archives/814394-crowded-orange-county-commission-races-get-whittled-down-to-runoffs/) and ClickOrlando (https://www.clickorlando.com/news/local/2026/09/04/orange-county-dist-2-candidates-talk-water-traffic-and-property-taxes-ahead-of-2026-runoff/).

candidates.name: Kamia Brown
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.background: Kamia Brown was born in Orlando in 1980 and earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Florida A&M University in 2003. She worked as a legislative assistant in the Florida Legislature before serving in the Florida House of Representatives for District 45 from 2016 to 2022. She lives in Ocoee and is running for the Orange County Commission in District 2.
candidates.primary_result: First in Aug 18 primary with just over 32%

taxes.summary: No public position found as of Sept 2026.

property_tax.summary: Ahead of the runoff, Brown criticized the state homestead-exemption amendment as packaged, calling it a tax shift onto local governments rather than relief, and said lawmakers should take more time on property-tax relief.
property_tax.quote: How this bill was packaged is not the way to go. It is not a property tax relief, it is a tax shift.

candidates.name: Mike Crabb
candidates.background: Advanced to the runoff as runner-up in the District 2 primary (other candidates: George Oliver III, Marsha Summersill, Wes Hodge).
candidates.primary_result: Second in Aug 18 primary with close to 26%

taxes.summary: Crabb's campaign website, quoted on Ballotpedia, lists economic affordability first among his priorities and says he will work to tackle housing costs, reduce taxes and attract high-paying jobs. It does not say which spending he would cut.
taxes.quote: Mike will work to tackle housing costs, reduce taxes, and attract high-paying jobs so families can afford to live, work, and thrive in Northwest Orange County.

sources.title: Mike Crabb campaign website, quoted on Ballotpedia

property_tax.summary: Crabb said he is concerned about the revenue the county could lose under the homestead-exemption amendment but that it is premature to decide on specific cuts; he called the potential deficits 'huge numbers.'
